_owner_decision: 2026-07-29, owner-ratified. The brace-expansion trap fired and MEASUREMENT redirected the fix. Chosen: SPLIT. This slice now covers next + postcss ONLY; brace-expansion is deliberately OUT and is closed as a consequence of the separate `eslint-10-migration` slice. WHY brace-expansion cannot be fixed here: GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg affects <= 5.0.7 with 5.0.8 as the ONLY patched release, so the v1 branch has no in-range fix. Forcing `brace-expansion@1` to ^5 does not merely cross a major -- it BREAKS AT RUNTIME: v1 is `module.exports = expandTop` (a function) while v5 CJS is `exports.expand` (an object), and the sole consumer minimatch@3.1.5 calls `require('brace-expansion')(...)` as a function. `pnpm install` resolves cleanly and lint dies at call time. WHY the eslint route is the real fix and why it is NOT this slice: eslint@9.39.4 itself depends on minimatch 3.1.5 (with @eslint/config-array@0.21.2 and @eslint/eslintrc@3.3.5), and ^9.18.0 already resolves to the newest 9.x, so nothing inside the ^9 range removes the v1 branch. ESLint v10.0.0 lists `501abd0 feat!: update dependency minimatch to v10 (#20246)` as a breaking change, so v10 drops the branch entirely. That is a major toolchain upgrade with its own compatibility surface (typescript-eslint, @next/eslint-plugin-next, Node floor ^20.19 || ^22.13 || >=24) and it is driven by ESLint v9 END-OF-LIFE on 2026-08-06, not by this advisory. Folding it in here would make this manifest's own `_scope_out` clause 'NO unrelated dependency upgrades riding along' meaningless. ACCEPTED COST: OSV stays red on brace-expansion for the few days between the two slices. Accepted because exposure is dev-only -- the v1 branch is reachable only through the eslint toolchain, has no runtime path, and its inputs are globs written by this team -- and because the alternative (an osv-scanner.toml ignore entry) leaves a suppression someone must remember to remove. SECOND SPLIT, 2026-07-30, owner-ratified: postcss is now ALSO OUT of this slice, deferred to a follow-up slice landing 8.5.23 directly. (a) WHY: the security-review round (gate-attempt-02, feature deps-security-bump--dsb7-rebaseline) independently reproduced a real, upstream-acknowledged issue in postcss 8.5.18 -- `postcss.parse`/`postcss.process` will read and return the bytes of a file at an attacker-named absolute path via a `sourceMappingURL` comment when `opts.from` is omitted, fixed by commit 7beca139e70f9075c6b19700fcb00dd8033e5da8 ('Does no load source map file without opts.from', 2026-07-24) and shipped in 8.5.23. Traced why the SAME round stayed silent on brace-expansion despite its real, tracked GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg: the security prompt is hard-coded in autopilot-review-readiness.mjs and passes the reviewer only `--base <sha>` plus a generic instruction -- no manifest, no scope, no owner decisions, no waiver mechanism of any kind. brace-expansion is silent purely because its lockfile lines are byte-unchanged and therefore absent from the diff; the reviewer never sees it to comment on it. The only way to stop the reviewer flagging postcss is for postcss not to be in the diff -- the same mechanism already used for brace-expansion, applied a second time. 8.5.23 was published 2026-07-24T17:04:03Z and minimumReleaseAge (10080 min / 7 days) does not clear it until 2026-07-31T17:04:03Z; per the 2026-07-26 decision above, only the owner may authorize an exception to that window, and none was granted -- the wait was chosen instead. (b) NOT A NEW EXPOSURE: `main` already sits at postcss 8.5.16 (the pre-bump baseline); deferring the 8.5.18->8.5.23 fix for ~26-29 hours leaves the tree no worse than main already is, and this slice's own DSB-1 (osv-scanner zero findings) was already scoped to next+postcss only and is now correctly narrowed to next -- postcss carries no CVE/GHSA/OSV record as of this investigation, so its continued advisory-absence is not a regression against any acceptance bar this slice ever promised. (c) PRESERVED FOR THE FOLLOW-UP, do not re-derive: fix-round-1 of this same lifecycle (before the split) found that pnpm-workspace.yaml's conditional override selector `postcss@<8.5.10: 8.5.16` (later widened to `<8.5.18: 8.5.18` before this revert) has a boundary hole -- a selector of `<8.5.10` does not catch a dependent that requests e.g. `postcss: ^8.5.12`, which is still inside the vulnerable range for the CURRENT advisory (GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849, which affects through 8.5.17) even though `^8.5.12` does not match `<8.5.10`. The follow-up slice must widen the selector to `<8.5.23` (or whatever the newly re-measured target version is) in BOTH package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml using the IDENTICAL scoped-selector key syntax (`"postcss@<TARGET": "TARGET"`), matching the pattern already proven in this lifecycle's own fix-round-1 (code-review [P2]: a bare unconditional `"postcss": "TARGET"` in package.json permanently caps every future consumer, so the key itself -- not just the value -- must carry the same conditional selector as pnpm-workspace.yaml). This is required work for the follow-up, not optional cleanup.
_round3_review_finding_investigated: 2026-07-30. Gate-attempt-03 code-review round 1 raised a [P1]: 'postcss remains vulnerable ... maintainer advisory affects all versions through 8.5.22; 8.5.23 is the complete fix', citing GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp. Verified against FOUR independent sources before treating this as a false positive, matching the invariant that a reviewer finding needs verification before being accepted OR dismissed: (1) `curl https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp` -> `{"code":5,"message":"Vulnerability not found"}` -- the cited GHSA ID does not exist. (2) `curl https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp` -> HTTP 404 on GitHub's own advisory API. (3) Direct OSV querybatch for `postcss@8.5.18` on npm -> `{}`, zero vulnerabilities. (4) `pnpm audit --json` (npm registry's own advisory database, a different pipeline than OSV) -> exactly 2 advisories total, esbuild and brace-expansion, zero postcss. The partial truth inside the finding: postcss 8.5.23's own GitHub release note (fetched via `api.github.com/repos/postcss/postcss/releases/tags/8.5.23`, published 2026-07-24T17:04:03Z) reads 'Do not load source map without opts.from for security reasons' -- a real maintainer hardening change, but as of this investigation it carries no CVE/GHSA/OSV record, i.e. it is not a disclosed, tracked vulnerability this slice's DSB-1 (osv-scanner zero findings) is scoped to close. Separately and independently of the truth of the claim: 8.5.23 was published 2026-07-24, six days before this run (2026-07-30) -- still inside the `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` (7-day) window, clearing 2026-07-31. Per `_timing_gate`'s owner decision 2026-07-26, any exception to that window requires 'a named per-package override with a reason and an expiry' authorized by the owner, not a unilateral agent decision, and doubly so when the only basis for the exception is an unverifiable claim. Conclusion at the time: DSB-1 as THEN written (osv-scanner reports zero findings for next and postcss) remained satisfied and was not redefined by this investigation; adopting 8.5.23 preemptively was deferred, not performed. UPDATE 2026-07-30: this investigation's own conclusion held for less than a day -- the very next gate round (security-review, feature deps-security-bump--dsb7-rebaseline) independently reproduced a REAL postcss issue by a different mechanism (file-read-without-opts.from, fixed in the same 8.5.23, but via a genuine upstream commit rather than a fabricated advisory). Owner then split postcss out of this slice entirely; DSB-1's CURRENT wording (see `_acceptance` above) covers next only. This entry is kept verbatim as the historical record of the round-3 hallucination and its correct handling (verify before dismissing); it does not describe the current acceptance bar. See `_owner_decision`'s SECOND SPLIT entry for the real finding and the current state.
